source.section: Form 80-105 page 1 lines 8-17 and page 2 lines 38-66; Instructions PDF p.5 Filing Status and Exemptions table; p.6 Additional Exemptions, Lines 8-12; p.7 Lines 14-17; p.22 Tax Rates; p.27 Schedule of Tax Computation lines 1-4; Instructions PDF p.11 Line 46 Total Pensions and Annuities; FAQ 'Is retirement income taxable?'; Miss. Admin. Code Title 35 Part III Subpart 02 Chapter 07 rules 100, 102 and 104 (https://www.sos.ms.gov/adminsearch/ACCode/00000158c.pdf, PDF p.18)

worked: Federal AGI = employer plan distribution (person 0) 60,000.00 = 60,000.00. Federal taxable income = 60,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 44,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form 80-105 filing status box 5, Single. Start at federal AGI 60,000.00 (Mississippi builds its own income on lines 38 to 66; the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt income, the same result here). Less retirement income 60,000.00 (exempt in total: regulation rule 102 counts a 401(k), 403(b) or 457 payout, tax deferred federally, as an optional retirement allowance when the recipient qualifies for other retirement income by minimum age, years of service or other criteria; rule 100 exempts it). Person 0 is 62 and is taken to have met the plan's age or service test; the projection cannot test it and exempts the payout at any age. Line 66 and line 13 Mississippi AGI = 0.00. Line 14 standard deduction 2,300.00. Line 8 age boxes checked 0; line 10 = 0 x 1,500.00 = 0.00; line 11 6,000.00; line 12 and line 15 = 6,000.00. Line 16 Mississippi taxable income = 0.00 - 2,300.00 - 6,000.00 = -8,300.00 on the formula; floored at 0.00 (the form enters 0). Schedule of Tax Computation lines 1 to 4 and line 17 = 0.00. Lines 18 and 19 credits 0.00; line 20 = 0.00. Before the 2026-11-07 decision this case taxed the payout (1,834.80).
accepted_approximations: Mississippi builds its own income (Form 80-105 lines 38 to 66); the projection starts from federal AGI and removes the exempt income through the reliefs and Social Security treatment.

IRA, 401(k), 403(b) and 457 payouts and Roth conversions are exempted at every age. Mississippi exempts them only when they are not early distributions (regulation rule 104), and a deferred compensation payout only once the person qualifies for other retirement income by minimum age, years of service or other criteria (rule 102). A projection cannot test either, so an early payout is exempted here; the warning names it for anyone under 60.
